design.note: The prompt names no authoring experience, and TWO outcomes are correct. (a) Leave the view unstated, yielding a `view` hole. (b) Map 'authoring… add questions… delete widgets' to item-edit, which then requires a `reference` the prompt never gave, yielding a `reference` hole. All four models measured on 2026-08-12 took (b); the dialect's own instruction is to map the request to the right view, and asking for a concrete reference is better steering than asking which of four views was meant. Either hole passes. What fails is a guessed view accompanied by an INVENTED reference — a design that reports complete, which is the one outcome this case exists to catch.

design.note: Starts complete and warning-free. Switching to item-list makes `reference` unnecessary and makes the `widget` and `settings` members invalid for the view — a browser has no widgets to edit. Carrying them over earns member-dropped warnings, which is the defect this case exists to catch.
